title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.30435v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. translated_title: 检索增强大语言模型中搜索状态感知的自评估强化学习
translated_abstract: 近年来搜索智能体的进展使大语言模型能够通过检索和综合外部信息来完成复杂任务。然而，现有搜索智能体往往缺乏搜索状态感知能力，即识别已经获取了哪些信息以及仍然缺少哪些信息的能力，这会导致幻觉式推理和过早终止搜索。为了解决这一局限，我们提出了自评估强化学习（SARL），这是一种强化学习框架，模型在训练过程中学习识别自身的搜索状态并据此改进搜索行为，而无需在测试时进行额外评估。SARL通过双重奖励设计来实现这一点：该设计既捕捉每次评估带来的纠正效果，又惩罚对评估的过度依赖，从而共同鼓励有效且高效的搜索轨迹。在此设置下，SARL相对基线实现了24.3%的相对提升（摘要原文在此处被截断）。
tldr: 提出SARL框架，通过兼顾评估纠正效果与惩罚过度依赖的双重奖励设计，让模型在训练中学会感知自身搜索状态，无需测试时额外评估即可实现更有效且高效的搜索，相比基线获得24.3%的相对提升。
en_tdlr: SARL is a reinforcement learning framework with a dual reward design that teaches models to recognize their own search state during training, enabling more effective and efficient search without extra assessment at test time, achieving a 24.3% relative improvement over baselines.
